Neon Retro Web fuses the structural logic of a systems dashboard with the electric color energy of neon-lit cyber aesthetics, producing a portfolio that reads as both technically serious and visually striking. Modular panels organize content with the precision of a terminal readout, while bright neon accents keep the whole interface buzzing with retro-futuristic life.

## Theme Overview

Neon Retro Web sits at the intersection of two powerful retro-computing aesthetics: the structured, information-dense world of terminal dashboards and the vivid, high-saturation color of neon cyberpunk design. The layout organizes portfolio content into distinct modular panels — each section self-contained and clearly delineated — giving the interface the legible, scannable quality of a well-designed status screen. Against this structural clarity, the neon color palette provides visual energy and personality, turning a portfolio into something that feels genuinely alive. Old-school terminal typography and subtle grid details reinforce the systems-engineering atmosphere throughout.

## Design Highlights

- Modular information panels that organize content with dashboard-style clarity
- Neon color palette that brings bright cyber energy to a dark interface ground
- Old-school terminal typography that reinforces the systems-dashboard identity
- Grid-based layout structure inspired by information-dense technical readouts
- A retro-futuristic design tone that balances technical authority with visual flair

## Who This Theme Suits

Neon Retro Web is an excellent match for systems engineers, DevOps professionals, security researchers, and back-end developers who want a portfolio that feels as technical as it looks distinctive. It also works well for developers who have a genuine affinity for cyberpunk or terminal aesthetics and want those sensibilities expressed in a professional context — someone whose GitHub profile and portfolio should feel part of the same design universe.

<Tip>
  Use Neon Retro Web's modular panel structure to give each major portfolio section — skills, projects, experience, contact — its own dedicated visual block, reinforcing the dashboard metaphor.
</Tip>
